The only torch.topk(k=2) is in the secondary low-margin mix, not a candidate cap. No env knob exists, and tools/build_probe_kernel.py has no patch for it (its PATCHES are gshift ... coordinject, none per-node). So it needs new predict-stage code and a new anchor, and it cannot be built or trusted in the ~35 min dummy budget with ~3 GPU hours and 2 slots left. (2) There is no lab gate: the exp60 dumps are post-relink, so any adoption would rest on a public read, which conflicts with the no-public-fitting condition in spirit, even though the 5/10 um value comes from the royerlab ultrack config. (3) The expected sign is <= 0 on an unseen embryo. The cap prunes ILP candidates in dense regions, and daughters are often the 2nd or 3rd candidate (739516: forks 88% vs continuations 99.7% coverage), so it risks division supply, and relink rewires the edges afterwards anyway. The adjacent outside read on this stage (imissher 743222, candidate threshold 0.48 -> 0.30) was 0.000 on the LB. Its node effect is unknown and not bounded to <1.5%.
